first.rationale:
The two declining metrics this quarter are activation (-6%) and onboarding completion (-4%), and the objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, not a short-term acquisition spike. That rules out the most tempting response to the competitor: memory_73 explicitly records that promotional pricing bought acquisition and revenue lift at the cost of materially worse 30-day retention, and explicitly warns against generalizing it. Chasing an entry-price competitor with discounting would trade exactly the durable revenue we are told to maximize. Referral incentives (memory_57) are clean but act on established customers and do nothing for the funnel that is actually degrading; enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) targets a segment that is not the one under pressure. That leaves the two funnel levers. Activation messaging (memory_91) is a downstream nudge, but if onboarding completion is falling, fewer accounts reach the point where messaging can act, so fixing the earlier stage should dominate. I therefore intend simplify_onboarding, which memory_86 (completion, time-to-value) and memory_31 (signup field reduction, durable first-week activation lift) both support, and which plausibly addresses both declining metrics with one experiment.

I am spending both verification pulls on memory_86 and memory_31 precisely because they are the load-bearing evidence for my chosen action, rather than on memories that would only confirm a path I have already rejected. Two things about them need checking. First, memory_31 is from day 12 and memory_86 from day 52, both consolidated summaries with archived sources; the current declines are recent and may have a different cause (traffic mix, a shipped product change, or the competitor drawing a lower-intent SMB cohort), in which case a prior lift in a different context may not replicate. Second, and more important, these memories report completion and activation lifts but say nothing about downstream qualified revenue. Cutting required signup fields can raise activation while degrading lead qualification and routing quality, which is the exact metric I am optimizing; a summary that only recorded top-of-funnel wins would hide that. The archived records should show whether retention and revenue quality were measured or merely unobserved.

Running at standard experiment scale with a holdout, not a broad rollout: the inherited evidence is consistent and directionally strong, but it is secondhand, unverified until the pulls come back, and does not establish the downstream effect I care about. I will instrument 30-day retention and qualified-pipeline quality per cohort alongside completion and activation, and treat the prior lifts as unconfirmed until the archive supports them. If verification shows the fields being cut carried qualification signal, I will narrow to a small guarded test or shift the slot to activation_messaging.

final.rationale:
Verification largely resolved the concern I flagged. exp_86 was not a top-of-funnel-only win: completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, so the onboarding shortening improved the downstream metric I care about rather than trading against it. exp_31 also measured downstream effects: signup +15%, activation +9%, qualified revenue +4%, with 30-day retention -1%. That small retention dip is the one real caution — it is the signature of slightly lower-intent accounts entering when signup friction drops — but it is an order of magnitude milder than the retention damage memory_73 records for promotional pricing, and it came with positive qualified revenue, so the net on my actual objective is favorable.

So I commit the slot to simplify_onboarding at standard experiment scale with a holdout. It is the only candidate that directly addresses both degrading metrics (completion -4%, activation -6%) with evidence that is now first-hand-verified on downstream revenue and retention. Promotional_pricing stays rejected: it is the intuitive answer to a competitor's entry pricing, but memory_73 explicitly records material 30-day retention loss and warns against generalizing it, and the objective here is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so it would buy the wrong number. Referral_incentive (memory_57) is clean but acts on established customers and leaves the broken funnel stage untouched. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) targets a segment that is not under pressure. Activation_messaging (memory_91) remains the strongest fallback and the natural next slot, but it is downstream of the stage that is leaking, so fixing onboarding first should raise the population it can act on.

Remaining uncertainty I am not papering over. Both records are confirmed but historical (day 52 and day 12), and neither tells me why activation and completion are falling now; if the cause is a shifted traffic mix or a lower-intent SMB cohort drawn by the competitor's pricing, a prior lift need not replicate. exp_31's replication is explicitly SMB-only, so I will scope the signup-field reduction to SMB and not extend it to segments where it was never validated. I will instrument 30-day retention and qualified-pipeline quality per cohort alongside completion and activation, and read the retention arm specifically for whether the -1% dip widens under current traffic. If retention degrades beyond the prior margin or qualified revenue turns negative, I stop and reallocate the next slot to activation_messaging rather than scaling this to broad rollout on a single quarter's result.
